results.summary: This design cycles through the characters of the string LAB11 on a 7-segment display, one character per clock cycle. It is built with Wokwi and uses gates and flip-flops to change the state of the LED segments to form the next character. The design takes a clock and reset input and drives the seven segment outputs. It is intended as a simple educational demonstration, and the documentation notes that characters are most readable at the lowest clock speed.

results.summary_before: This project implements the Intel MCS-4 4004 CPU in Verilog, intended for use in a replica of the 141-PF calculator. The design can be configured in three ways: as an internal CPU within an FPGA, as an FPGA-based CPU connected to external MCS-4 system components, or as a standalone chip connected to an FPGA-based MCS-4 system. The chip requires external ROM and RAM to function as a complete system, and the documentation describes a debug system using an FPGA and a RISC-V subsystem for chip selection.
results.summary: This project implements the Intel MCS-4 4004 CPU in Verilog, intended for use in a replica of the 141-PF calculator. The design can be configured in three ways: as an internal CPU within an FPGA, as an FPGA-based CPU connected to external MCS-4 system components, or as a standalone chip connected to an FPGA-based MCS-4 system. The chip requires external ROM and RAM to function as a complete system, and the documentation describes a debug system using an FPGA and a RISC-V subsystem for chip selection. The design runs at 750 kHz and exposes data, sync and chip-select pins for the MCS-4 bus.
